entries.why: Attribution on DISCOVERY (H1 look20 buf0.0 atr1 hold12, 6,678 trades) showed stop-hit trades are 56.4% of the book and account for -4,066.6R, while full-hold time exits earn +2.5212R each. Losers reached only 0.726R MFE before dying at 1.407R MAE, i.e. they were killed while still near entry, not after a real move against them.
entries.change: Same signal rule, same hold, same session deadline, same cost. Stop moves from 1x ATR to 2x ATR. R is renormalised to the new risk, so E(R) stays comparable under fixed-fractional sizing.
entries.criterion: Paired per-signal difference (variant minus baseline on signals BOTH arms take) must beat the declared margin, and its block-bootstrap t must clear the cumulative-k floor.
entries.test_period: HOLDOUT H1 2017-01-01 onwards - the attribution that suggested this ran on discovery only

result.note: Win rate rose 33.4%->44.0% and 3,601 of 5,455 signals improved against 1,854 worsened, yet the net is +0.0010R. The wider stop converts many small losses into small wins and makes the remaining losses proportionally larger; the money nets out. Separately: the baseline itself earns -0.0001R on holdout against +0.0175R on discovery, so the config being improved has no edge to improve.

entries.why: Arithmetic, not a pattern: the spread is fixed at 0.260 price units regardless of horizon, so the only way to raise the gross edge against it is a larger move. The first test proved the stop cannot do this - it scales the edge and the cost by the same factor. Hold is the other lever. DISCLOSURE: I have already seen the holdout cost decomposition for atr1/atr2, so this test is not fully blind. Recorded here rather than hidden.
entries.change: Same signal rule, same atr1 stop, same session deadline, same cost. hold_max moves from 12 bars to 24. The 20:30 UTC force-close still binds first on most trades, so the effective change is smaller than 12 to 24 suggests.
entries.criterion: Paired per-signal difference on shared signals must beat the declared margin, and its block-bootstrap t must clear the cumulative-k floor.
entries.test_period: HOLDOUT H1 2017-01-01 onwards

result.note: The session deadline binds first: 4,886 of 5,455 trades were UNCHANGED because the 20:30 UTC force-close already closed them before bar 12. Of the 569 that could move, 255 improved and 314 worsened. The horizon lever is not available on an intraday setup - rule 6 (force close before rollover) caps it structurally, so raising hold_max on H1 changes almost nothing and what it does change is slightly worse.

entries.why: User's argument: one strict setup firing once a month is unmeasurable, but 100 equally strict setups reach 70+ signals a month, which IS tradeable. Acknowledged upfront that it would be overfit, but proposed the result might still be positive. The frequency half of this is correct and setup_power.py answered the wrong question by treating one setup in isolation.
entries.change: Take the frozen 176-cell grid in multi_tf_setup_grid.py WHOLE (11 entry families x params x 4 exits x 2 stops). Select cells on DISCOVERY only by six declared rules, then measure those same cells on HOLDOUT as one pooled portfolio, block-bootstrapped over time so cross-cell overlap is carried, and against a matched control that preserves direction mix and exit design but randomises entry timing.
entries.criterion: The pooled holdout book must beat zero with a block-bootstrap t clearing the floor for the number of selection rules tried, AND show skill over the timing-destroyed control.
entries.test_period: HOLDOUT H1 2017-01-01 onwards; selection used DISCOVERY 2004-2017 only

result.note: Best rule was keep-t>2: 28 cells, holdout E +0.0269R. Baseline here is the matched control (+0.0029) since the question is entry skill, not raw return. Naive t was +3.12 but collapsed to +1.00 once cross-cell overlap was carried - 28 cells trading the same gold on the same bars are not 28 independent samples. Skill over the timing-destroyed control is +0.0240 at block t +0.90. NOT flat zero the way pure selection is (Part 1 null gives 0.0000 regardless of strictness), so something is carried from discovery to holdout - but it is indistinguishable from noise and 57% of the selected cells are Donchian breakout, the family cross_market.py independently closed on 9 of 9 markets.

entries.why: User's refinement: do not loosen the rare setup - make it STRICTER still, and run enough strict setups to reach 60 signals a month. The existing four-stage ablation supports the premise: E rises monotonically with depth (-0.091, +0.001, +0.039, +0.296) and the stated reason row 4 is not a result is that its MDE exceeds its effect, which is a SAMPLE SIZE objection that breadth legitimately answers.
entries.change: Build conjunctions BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by selection: every combination of k conditions from a fixed 13-condition library, depths 1 to 4, nothing dropped for looking bad or for being rare. Pool all trades at each depth. Compare against two nulls - time-shuffled conditions (same rarity, no information) and randomised timing (same directions, same drift, no timing claim).
entries.criterion: Skill over the timing control must RISE with depth and clear the floor for the number of depths tried.
entries.test_period: HOLDOUT H1 2017-01-01 onwards

result.note: Baseline is depth 1 skill, variant is depth 4 skill - the question was whether strictness RAISES skill. It does not: skill runs +0.0200, +0.0206, +0.0261, +0.0159 across depths 1-4, flat and never significant (t +0.77, +0.61, +0.63, +0.33 against a 1.67 floor). Raw E does rise (+0.0218 to +0.0544) and time-shuffled conditions do NOT reproduce that rise - but the randomised-TIMING control does, rising +0.0017 to +0.0384. So the rise is a sampling-density effect of sparse signals, not information in the conditions. Separately, every depth's skill is below the 0.0518R round-trip cost at a 1.5 ATR stop.

entries.why: combinatorics.py measured that the 131,040-cell nominal space is only of order 751 effectively independent questions (m_eff = 3.69 k^0.451, fitted on measured return-series correlation). So the whole space can be probed at 751 tests rather than 131,040, and the honest multiple-testing floor is sqrt(2 ln 751) = 3.64 rather than 4.85. Running the representatives is cheap and the floor is already known.
entries.change: Stratified random sample of 751 cells across depth 1-6 x 4 exits x 2 stops x 4 timeframes, seed 17 fixed and declared. NOTHING is chosen by performance - the strata and the seed fully determine the sample. Each cell measured on its own timeframe's discovery split, then the same cell measured on holdout. Skill is taken against a randomised-TIMING control, not raw E, because strictness.py showed raw E carries a signal-density artefact that a random-timing book reproduces.
entries.criterion: A cell PASSES only if its discovery skill t clears 3.64 AND its holdout skill is positive. Both, declared now. The pooled all-751 book is reported alongside as the no-selection baseline.
entries.test_period: Per timeframe: H1 discovery 2004-2017 / holdout 2017-2026; M5-M30 discovery to 2023 / holdout 2023-2026

result.note: 324 of 751 cells produced a usable book on both periods. Distribution of discovery skill t is OVER-DISPERSED (mean +0.155, sd 1.475 against noise 0 and 1; max +4.66, min -5.79) so the space is not dead - but the dispersion is symmetric, the signature of effects strong within a period and reversing between them. 3 cells cleared the 3.64 floor on discovery, 1 was also positive on holdout: fast_ema+in_fvg+mom_50 on H1 trail-2ATR-BE, discovery skill +0.1214 t+4.66, holdout skill +0.0265 t+0.87. Decisive number is the rank test: corr(discovery t, holdout skill) over 318 cells is Pearson -0.016 (-0.3 SE) and Spearman +0.102 (+1.8 SE), neither clearing 2 SE, and the WORST discovery quintile has higher mean holdout skill (+0.0166) than the best (+0.0042). No-selection baseline is E -0.0707 discovery, -0.0502 holdout.

entries.why: Four commercial KRV EAs supplied as compiled .ex5 (no source, high entropy, no readable logic). The EAs themselves cannot be read, but the four FAMILIES their names describe can each be implemented from a standard textbook definition and tested. A dead family is strong evidence against any implementation of it; a live family would justify asking the vendor for the .mq5.
entries.change: Implement four families from standard definitions: (1) regular price/RSI divergence reversal, (2) range compression then breakout of the compressed range, (3) exhaustion reversal after an extended run plus a climax bar, (4) tick-volume profile POC/value-area zones. Each at 3 declared parameter variants x 2 exit designs. Skill measured against a randomised-timing control. Discovery then holdout, block-bootstrapped.
entries.criterion: A family survives only if at least one variant clears the floor for 24 tests on DISCOVERY and keeps positive skill on HOLDOUT, and its skill exceeds the round-trip cost.
entries.test_period: H1 XAUUSD, discovery 2004-2017, holdout 2017-2026

result.note: All four families fail the registered three-part criterion. Best is compression (n=12,q=0.20, stop+time): discovery skill +0.3624 at t+3.61, clears the 2.52 floor, but holdout skill collapses to +0.0423 at t+0.41 - BELOW the 0.0518R round-trip cost, so baseline here is the cost itself. Compression is coherent on discovery (3 of 6 variants above t+3.0) and gone on holdout (+0.0423, +0.0241, +0.0173, -0.0156, -0.0124, -0.1490). divergence best t_d +1.42, exhaustion best t_d -0.24 (negative skill on every variant), volume_poc best t_d +2.51 - none clears. NOTE: these are reimplementations from the family names, NOT tests of the compiled .ex5 binaries, whose logic is unrecoverable. Evidence runs one way only: dead family is evidence against any build of it; a live one would only justify requesting the .mq5.

entries.why: The vendor supplied full written specifications for all four EAs. My first implementation (vendor_four_families, REJECTED) was materially wrong against those specs: Volume Power Zones is a volume-weighted ORDER BLOCK with an ATR-x4 displacement trigger and a retest, not a volume profile POC - I implemented the wrong strategy entirely. Exhaustion omitted its core mechanism, declining volume through the run plus a shift bar on ABOVE-average volume. Divergence omitted Hidden divergence and every trend filter, which the docs single out as the biggest win-rate lever. Compression omitted BBW, the minimum squeeze duration, the impulse-body test and the volume surge. The previous REJECTED verdict therefore does not stand as a test of these families.
entries.change: Reimplement all four to the written specs. Divergence: Regular AND Hidden, with and without an HTF EMA trend gate. Compression: BBW and ATR both below their own rolling means for a minimum number of bars, range box, close breakout plus impulse body, with and without volume surge. Exhaustion: 4-9 bar run with declining relative volume, then an opposite shift bar on above-average volume with a body-ratio and close-position test. Volume Power Zones: confirmed swing pivots weighted by volume against a 20-bar volume MA, ATR-x4 displacement trigger, retest of the block with a cooldown. 10 signal configurations x 2 exits.
entries.criterion: A family survives only if at least one configuration clears the floor for 20 tests on DISCOVERY, keeps positive skill on HOLDOUT, and its holdout skill exceeds the round-trip cost. All three, as before.
entries.test_period: H1 XAUUSD, discovery 2004-2017, holdout 2017-2026

result.note: ONE configuration meets the registered three-part criterion: compression, min_bars=6 impulse=1.0 vol_surge=True, 1leg 2R BE. Discovery skill +0.1564 at t+3.58 (clears the 2.52 floor, 1,023 trades); holdout skill +0.0999 at t+1.93 (positive, and above the 0.0518R cost, 785 trades). Baseline here is the cost itself. The volume surge is what did it and it is a filter from the vendor's own documentation, not something searched for: without it t_d +2.63/+1.36 and holdout -0.0701/-0.0471; with it t_d +3.58/+4.07 and holdout +0.0999/-0.0073. Caveats: 1 of 24 tests, holdout t does not itself clear the floor, and the 3leg sister config of the same signal is negative on holdout. Ran 24 tests not the 20 registered (12 configs x 2 exits, not 10) - floor 2.52 rather than 2.45, stricter than registered. Everything else dead: div_regular best t_d +2.49, div_hidden +0.65, exhaustion +2.05, power_zones +0.89.

entries.why: One configuration cleared all three parts of the vendor_families_v2 criterion: compression with vol_surge=True at 1leg 2R BE, discovery skill +0.1564 t+3.58, holdout skill +0.0999 t+1.93 against a 0.0518R cost. The volume surge is the vendor's own documented filter, not a searched parameter, and turning it on flipped holdout from -0.0701 to +0.0999. It is still 1 of 24 tests on one instrument, and this repo's standing rule is that an effect found on gold and absent elsewhere is gold overfit.
entries.change: Freeze that exact rule - BBW and ATR both under their rolling means for 6 bars, range box, close breakout with body >= 1.0 ATR, volume above 1.2x its 20-bar mean, 1.5 ATR stop, single 2R target with break-even - and run it unchanged on all nine markets, each charged its own measured median spread. No parameter is refitted per market. For the eight non-gold markets every bar is out of sample, since none of their data was used to find the rule.
entries.criterion: Pre-declared at the same bar cross_market.py already uses: the rule REPLICATES only if skill is positive on at least 8 of 9 markets (binomial P = 1.95%). 7 of 9 is suggestive and is NOT a pass. Markets are not independent, so the binomial figure is an upper bound on the evidence.
entries.test_period: Full history per market, 2003-2026, H1

result.note: REPLICATES at the pre-declared bar: positive skill on 8 of 9 markets, P=0.0195 (t recorded is the binomial-equivalent z of 2.06). Mean skill +0.0333, median +0.0364, four markets at t>2 (gold +2.78, EURUSD +2.68, USDJPY +2.42, GBPUSD +2.12). The eight non-gold markets are out of sample in every respect and are positive on 7 of 8. This is the first rule in the project to replicate cross-market. BUT SKILL IS NOT PROFIT and here they come apart: E(R) is positive on only 2 of 9 (EURUSD +0.0137 at t+0.42, USDJPY +0.0235 at t+0.64) and NOTHING is significantly profitable anywhere. The cost relationship is real - slope -1.5070, and it survives removing XAGUSD (slope -0.5983) - but the zero-cost intercept falls from +0.0759 to +0.0143 once silver is dropped, so most of the apparent gross edge was that one point. +0.0143 is indistinguishable from zero. Reading: the entry carries genuine information about timing, replicated across nine markets, and not enough of it to pay a spread anywhere.

entries.why: HONESTLY NOT BLIND: found via debugging the vendor's 25-template spec (xauusd_1000_setups.py). P01 (Donchian-20 breakout) on M15 2019-2026 real bid/ask cleared the baseline floor after a control-bug fix, and is the SAME family cross_market.py already declared dead 9/9 markets under a different spec (SL=1.5xATR, TP=2R, 12-bar hold, flat 260pt cost). This spec differs materially: SL from the signal bar's own low/high + buffer, TP=1R, 24-bar hold, REAL bid/ask fill (Buy@Ask/Sell@Bid) instead of mid minus a flat spread. Extended to full H1 2004-2026 it gave discovery skill +0.1094 t+3.70, holdout skill +0.1046 t+4.42, both periods gross E(R) positive (+0.0538, +0.0856). That is the best number this project has ever produced if real, and results this good after this many dead ends are the ones most likely to hide a bug - which is exactly why this is registered before being trusted rather than reported.
entries.change: Freeze the P01 spec exactly (Donchian-20 breakout, TP=1R from real fill, SL=bar low/high minus buffer, 24-bar time exit, tick-rounded, G09 pre-trade gate) and run it unchanged, real bid/ask, on all 9 markets this repo has H1 bid/ask for. No refitting per market.
entries.criterion: Same bar as every prior cross-market test in this project: skill positive on at least 8 of 9 markets (binomial P=1.95%), AND gross E(R) positive on at least 6 of 9 (since this project's standing lesson is that skill and profit are different claims and skill alone was not enough for the compression rule).
entries.test_period: Full H1 history per market, 2004-2026

result.note: RETRACTED BY ITS OWN CALIBRATION. The pre-fix run met both halves of the declared criterion spectacularly: skill positive 9 of 9 on both periods (P=0.0020), gross E(R) positive 9 of 9, t up to +9.68. It was a one-bar look-ahead. Entry used ask_CLOSE of bar t+1 while the exit loop scanned that same bar's high and low, so trades could be resolved by price action that happened before they were entered; the spec says 'Ask แรกของแท่ง t+1' - the OPEN. Caught by running the rule on mega_search.synth martingale data, where a correct engine must return skill 0 and E(R) = minus the spread: it returned skill +0.0728 (t up to +5.02) and E(R) +0.0034. After the fix the same synthetic calibration returns skill +0.0016 and E(R) -0.0590, and the nine real markets collapse to skill positive 5 of 9 (a coin flip), gross E(R) positive 0 of 9, mean E(R) -0.0652. Two further real fixes were made in the same pass: exits were tested against MID highs and lows while entries filled at the real ask, charging half a spread instead of a whole one; and the random-timing control used a fixed 1.5xATR stop against a rule whose stop ranges 0.3-3 ATR, so R had different denominators in the two books. Neither of those was the main defect. The 13-template M15 baseline re-run with the fixed engine has 0 of 13 clearing the floor.

entries.why: README marks Setup D as the ONE hypothesis that survived this project's own 16-round research: (Close-SMA200)/ATR in [1.08,7.21], permutation p=0.0005, net E +0.2312R at 8R. It is the EA's only default-ON setup. Config.mqh states plainly 'NOT YET VALIDATED: the zone was found on the FULL gold sample, not a held-out half, and cross-asset confirmation (silver, EURUSD) has not been run. If it does not reproduce there, this is gold overfit.' That test has never been run. Separately, the README's own drift table shows longs-in-zone skill is NEGATIVE after subtracting drift (-0.0494, t-4.14) while the default config trades ONLY longs - so the side being traded is the side whose raw edge is drift.
entries.change: Implement Setup D exactly: z=(Close-SMA200)/ATR, long [1.08,7.21] short [-7.21,-1.08], fire only on ENTERING the zone, flat 1.8 ATR stop, 8R target, 30-hour time stop, one position at a time, real bid/ask fill at the entry bar's open quote. Two runs: (1) gold M15 to verify the implementation reproduces the documented result before anything else is believed, (2) all 9 markets on H1 with the time stop matched in wall-clock hours. Report raw E AND drift-adjusted skill per market per side.
entries.criterion: Cross-asset validation as Config.mqh itself defines it: the zone must reproduce outside gold. Declared bar - DRIFT-ADJUSTED skill positive on at least 8 of 9 markets for whichever side is traded (binomial P=1.95%), AND the gold M15 verification run must land within a factor of two of the documented +0.2312R at 8R, otherwise the implementation is wrong and nothing else in the run counts.
entries.test_period: gold M15 2019-2026 for verification; 9 markets H1 2004-2026 for cross-asset

result.note: Does NOT replicate. Drift-adjusted skill positive on 0 of 9 markets on BOTH sides (declared bar was 8 of 9 on the long side). Long mean skill -0.1322 (across-market t -2.97), short -0.1226 (t -3.51). Only USDJPY long had positive raw E (+0.0557) and its skill was -0.0535 - the market went up, measured twice. Gold itself is in the failing set: XAUUSD H1 long E -0.0994, skill -0.1055. Implementation verified first: gold M15 reproduces +0.1788R at zero cost against the documented +0.2312R (which README's own table says was costed at the $0.26 terminal quote), within the declared factor of two; at real measured bid/ask the same book is +0.0439R. So the gap is cost, not a coding error, and the nine-market result is a genuine test. This is exactly the outcome Config.mqh warned about. Note also that README's own drift table already showed the long side - the ONLY side the shipped config trades - has NEGATIVE drift-adjusted skill on gold itself (-0.0494, t -4.14), while the side with positive skill (shorts, +0.1092, t +7.56) is switched off.

entries.why: Every test in this repo - 33 topics, 40 files - runs at M1 to H1, where the measured round-turn spread is 5% to 57% of ATR (mean 19.0%). Nothing has ever gone UP the timeframe. Measured just now on the same caches: the same cost is 4.18% of ATR at D1 and 1.19% at W1 - a 5.3x and 16x reduction. Every candidate this project has killed died on cost, and the one lever that moves cost by an order of magnitude has never been pulled. Separately, this is the first hypothesis here that comes from OUTSIDE the data: time-series momentum (Moskowitz/Ooi/Pedersen 2012, 58 futures 1965-2009; extended to 1880 by Hurst/Ooi/Pedersen) is the most replicated anomaly in this space, and its prediction is made before the run rather than found by searching this sample.
entries.change: Resample H1 bid/ask to D1 for 10 markets, 2004-2026. At each month end take the sign of the trailing k-month mid-close return, k in {1,3,6,12}. Enter at the OPEN of the first trading day of the next month (ask for long, bid for short) and exit at the CLOSE of its last trading day (bid for long, ask for short). Non-overlapping monthly holds. Size to constant ex-ante volatility using an exponentially-weighted daily vol estimated only from data up to the signal, so R = realised return / ex-ante monthly vol. Decompose per market: raw E(R) = mean(d*x), drift term = mean(d)*mean(x), skill = covariance(d,x) - the genuine timing component. Build the equal-weight cross-market portfolio month by month so the pooled t accounts for cross-market correlation rather than assuming 10 independent tests. Swap = 0 in the main test per this project's cost rules, with a separate overnight report using the known XAUUSDc swap of -534.9 points.
entries.criterion: At the 12-month lookback - the literature's headline specification, fixed before the run - drift-adjusted skill positive on at least 8 of 10 markets AND the equal-weight portfolio's net-of-cost t clearing the multiple-testing floor.
entries.test_period: 10 markets D1 2004-2026 (XAUUSD, XAGUSD, USDSEK, EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD, NZDUSD). No entry rule in this repo was ever fitted at D1 or on a monthly hold, so the whole timeframe is out of sample with respect to every prior search here.

result.note: DOES NOT CLEAR. At the headline 12-month lookback the equal-weight portfolio makes +0.0248R/month, t +0.74, annualised Sharpe +0.13, and drift-adjusted skill is positive on 6 of 10 markets (binomial P 0.377, itself an upper bound since seven share the dollar). Declared bar was 8 of 10 plus a portfolio t clearing 3.66; both fail. The sweep is monotone in the literature's own direction (1m -0.0458 t -3.01, 3m -0.0439, 6m -0.0121, 12m +0.0248) - short-horizon reversal, long-horizon momentum - so the SIGN structure replicates while the magnitude does not survive this floor. Gold is again mostly drift: raw +0.2028 (t +2.29) splits into drift +0.1295 and skill +0.0852 (t +0.96), the same shape as Setup D. TWO FINDINGS THAT OUTLIVE THIS TEST. First, the cost premise was half right and half backwards: spread does collapse at D1 (gold 0.0119R/trade) but swap explodes (0.2498R/trade, 21x the spread), taking gold from +0.2028R to -0.0470R. Going up the timeframe trades a small cost problem for a larger one. Second, and it is closed form: with spread S paid once and swap w paid per night against a move growing like sqrt(h), cost/move is minimised at h* = S/w, with volatility cancelling entirely. For XAUUSDc long that is 0.4540/0.5349 = 0.85 nights. The cost-optimal hold for a gold long on this account is under one night, which means the premise of this file was wrong before the first trade was simulated - and the H1/H4 horizons this project has always used are not a habit but close to the only viable window. The asymmetry is unexploited: a gold short receives financing, so h* does not exist on that side, and this repo has worked the long side throughout.

entries.why: The repo inventory marks the real news calendar as never touched - turn-of-month died and the Friday-late replication failed at p=0.23, but no scheduled macro event has ever been looked at. Every one of the 40 files here tests a PRICE-PATTERN rule, asking whether a shape in past prices predicts the next move; forty files in, the answer is no. A calendar rule asks a different question - whether the cost and volatility environment changes at a KNOWN clock time - and that is a microstructure fact rather than a discovered pattern. This project's binding constraint has been cost throughout, so a measured change in cost at predictable times is worth more than another entry rule, whichever way it comes out.
entries.change: Build the NFP calendar with zero external data and zero recall risk: first Friday of each month at 08:30 America/New_York converted to UTC through zoneinfo, so US daylight saving is handled by the tz database rather than assumed. CALIBRATION FIRST, as with the martingale test - if the constructed calendar does not show a large spread and volatility spike at those bars, the calendar is wrong and nothing after it counts. Then for each event, normalise against a LOCAL control: the median spread and median |return|/ATR at the SAME UTC hour on non-event weekdays within +/-45 days, so hour-of-day and slow regime drift are both controlled. Report the spread multiple, the volatility multiple, and the ratio between them - the ratio is the decisive number, because a window where volatility expands faster than spread is a better place to trade despite the wider quote, and one where it does not is a trap. Finally test direction: sign of the event bar, entered at the OPEN of the FOLLOWING bar at real ask/bid, held 1/2/4/8 hours, both continuation and reversal.
entries.criterion: Two separate claims. STRUCTURAL: the volatility-to-spread ratio at the event bar differs from its local control by at least 20% in the same direction on at least 8 of 10 markets. DIRECTIONAL: net-of-cost E(R) positive with a block-bootstrap t clearing the multiple-testing floor at a single pre-chosen horizon, not the best of eight.
entries.test_period: 10 markets H1 2004-2026, roughly 264 NFP events each; XAUUSD M1 2019-2026 for the fine structure. No rule in this repo was ever fitted to event times, so the event partition is out of sample with respect to every prior search here.

result.note: SPLIT RESULT. Calibration passed: the calendar built from first-Friday plus zoneinfo locates real volatility spikes, 1.3x to 2.5x the local control on 9 of 10 markets, so the partition measures what it claims. STRUCTURAL CLAIM PASSES, with a caveat written before recording. The H1 spread column came back 1.00x on all ten markets, which is a measurement failure not a finding - an H1 bar's spread is its close quote, ninety minutes after the release - so it was discarded and redone on gold M1. There: spread 1.20x in the first five minutes against volatility 2.67x, a ratio of 2.23x, decaying to 1.37x by the first hour. That is the best movement-per-cost ratio measured anywhere in this project. The caveat is that the registered criterion tested the wrong cost: an M1 close is still a snapshot so 1.20x is a lower bound, slippage rather than spread dominates at a release and this project's own rules model it at at most 0.3x of spread which is far too low there, and requotes are not modelled at all. The 2.23x is an optimistic bound, not a tradeable number. DIRECTIONAL CLAIM FAILS. Gross E(R) at one hour is +0.0020 - nothing - and every longer horizon is worse (4h gross -0.0707). Net of cost, the pre-chosen 4h horizon gives E -0.2161R with t -2.29 on 272 event-day means, well short of the 3.66 floor and the wrong sign besides. The t is computed on event-day means across markets rather than on 9,713 pooled trades, since ten markets reacting to one release is one observation. So the release window concentrates opportunity without creating direction: the best place this project has found to PUT a signal, and there is no signal to put there. One reusable detail: the quoted spread peaks at -1 minute, BEFORE the release, and is already under 1.5x by the release minute - dealers widen defensively into a known time and normalise immediately, so anything that must transact near a scheduled release is cheaper doing it on the number than in the minute before it.

entries.why: The stage-1 liquidity sweep is the last candidate in this repo that has not collapsed: RESEARCH_FINDINGS records skill +0.051 at t +1.89 on 27 futures, H1, 730 days, and says it is 'the only smart-money primitive in this repo that has not flipped sign'. Two things about that record need settling. FIRST, it was measured at ZERO COST and its expectancy there is -0.091 - the rule loses money before a single spread is charged, so positive skill means random timing loses more, not that the rule earns. It has never been run at real bid/ask. SECOND, the repo contradicts itself: choch_fvg_three_setups.py line 41 states a sign flip 'disqualified the liquidity sweep, the strongest candidate in the program', while RESEARCH_FINDINGS line 911 states it did not flip sign. Both cannot be true and the difference decides whether this candidate is alive.
entries.change: Take the stage-1 rule VERBATIM from dobby_setup01_sweep_chain.py with no re-tuning - a wick clears the prior 20-bar extreme, the body closes back inside, penetration between 0.08 and 1.50 ATR - and feed it as dvec/Ivec into run_e01, the engine that carries the martingale calibration guard and the two look-ahead corrections. Ten markets, H1, 2004-2026, real Dukascopy bid/ask, entry at the entry bar's OPEN, exits tested on the side that closes the trade. Report raw E, drift-adjusted skill against run_e01_control with matched count, direction mix and risk ratios, per market and as a time-pooled equal-weight portfolio so cross-market overlap is inside the standard error rather than assumed away. Add Deflated Sharpe and a calibration run on martingale data that must show E<0 and skill~0 before any real number is read.
entries.criterion: POWERED TO REFUTE, NOT TO CONFIRM - and that is computed before the run, not discovered after. At the original signal rate of 3.84% of bars, this data yields about 68,000 trades and a projected t of 3.66 against a floor of 4.72; clearing the floor would need 113,000 trades. So the declared bar is a KILL bar: the candidate dies if drift-adjusted skill turns negative on the pooled sample, OR is positive on fewer than 6 of 10 markets, OR expectancy at real bid/ask stays negative. It SURVIVES - not accepted, survives - only if skill stays positive and consistent AND expectancy at real cost turns positive, which would make it the first rule in this repo to be both at once.
entries.test_period: 10 markets H1 2004-2026 at real bid/ask. The original measurement was 27 futures over 730 days at zero cost, so this shares no data with it beyond the overlap of gold and silver, and it is the first time the rule meets a spread at all.

result.note: KILLED on the pre-declared third condition. Calibration passed first: on an information-free random walk the rule returns E -0.0749 (the spread, which is the only edge available there) and skill +0.0104 (none). It also caught a real bug on the first run - run_e01_control returns a three-tuple, not an array of returns, and averaging the tuple gave skill -9975.87; the guard refused to print anything below it. Result on 9 markets, H1, 2004-2026, 43,198 trades at real bid/ask: pooled E -0.1040 with an overlap-aware block-bootstrap t of -21.75 (naive t -22.10). The two conditions that could have kept it alive both held - drift-adjusted skill is +0.0283 and positive on 9 of 9 markets - and the one that mattered failed. THE SIGN DID NOT FLIP, and that settles a contradiction in this repo's own source: choch_fvg_three_setups.py line 41 states a sign flip 'disqualified the liquidity sweep, the strongest candidate in the program', while RESEARCH_FINDINGS line 911 states it did not. Measured here at real cost the skill is +0.0283 against +0.051 at zero cost - same sign, smaller. Line 41 is wrong and is corrected in this commit. What actually kills the rule is what the zero-cost measurement could never see: the skill is real, small and consistent, and it is worth about a quarter of the spread it has to pay. Beating a random-timing control by +0.028R while losing -0.104R per trade is a statement about the control, not a reason to trade. Deflated Sharpe is 0.0000 at one trial and at k=824 alike - the sign is so firmly negative that deflation is not even the binding consideration. Power was declared before the run as unable to confirm (projected t 3.66 against a floor of 4.72) and that limitation never bound, because the result refutes rather than confirms.

entries.why: Twelve tests in this ledger and 824 hypotheses have produced no acceptance, and discipline_audit.py showed why further searching of the same nine markets cannot: the floor is now 4.72 and the smallest Sharpe 22 years can establish is 0.68, above the SG CTA Index's own realised 0.61 since 2000. The sample is spent. But the floor counts hypotheses spent BEFORE the evidence was seen, and that is the part this project had been applying too bluntly. Rules searched on data ALREADY burned, with one small set of finalists fixed in a file and then tested ONCE against a universe never examined, cost the holdout no significance - the selection consumed no holdout information. That is ordinary train/test logic and it is what makes a large search affordable again.
entries.change: Fetch fourteen FX crosses with no USD leg, 2012-2026 H1, never fetched or plotted in this repo, and seal them with a sha256 per file. Search 21,889 rules on the nine burned markets: twelve causal features cut at five of their own quantiles from both sides, ANDed at depths one to three, scored on overlap-adjusted t of signed forward return per ATR entered at the next bar's open. Calibrate the screen against a SIMULATED null - eight independent information-free walks through the identical screen - rather than any closed form, because the score distribution is heavy-tailed. Run survivors through run_e01 at ZERO COST first, since venue_change.py showed this repo's best candidate losing 0.0574R frictionless and a rule negative there is dead at every venue. Select at most three finalists by a criterion written into the source before any result existed: zero-cost E>0 on at least 7 of 9 markets, pooled skill>0 against the matched random-timing control, ranked by pooled zero-cost E. Then open the sealed crosses exactly once, with the script refusing a second run and verifying every hash.
entries.criterion: On the sealed crosses, a finalist must show positive E(R) at real bid/ask with an across-market |t| above the expected maximum of three draws, about 1.02. Not 4.72: the 21,889 rules were selected on data already spent and only the three finalists are ever charged against the untouched universe. If nothing clears - or if no finalist is nominated because nothing passed the zero-cost gate - that is the result and there is no second opening.
entries.test_period: DISCOVERY: the nine already-burned markets, XAUUSD/XAGUSD and seven majors, H1 2004-2026. HOLDOUT: fourteen FX crosses (EURJPY GBPJPY AUDJPY CHFJPY CADJPY NZDJPY EURGBP EURCHF EURAUD EURCAD AUDNZD AUDCAD GBPCHF GBPAUD) H1 2012-2026, never fetched, plotted, or tabulated in this repo, and sharing no USD leg with the discovery set.

result.note: NO FINALIST NOMINATED. The sealed universe was never opened, which the registered criterion names as a valid outcome rather than a failure to reach one. Two independent gates both returned nothing. THE SIMULATED NULL. 21,889 rules - twelve causal features cut at five of their own quantiles from both sides, ANDed at depths one to three - scored on nine markets over 23 years as overlap-adjusted t of signed forward return per ATR entered at the next bar's open. 17,136 fired on seven or more markets. The best scored 2.061. Eight independent information-free random walks through the identical screen produced maxima of 2.53, 2.68, 2.72, 2.42, 2.50, 2.41, 2.30 and 2.12, so the best real rule in the space does not reach even the WEAKEST of the eight null runs. Zero rules cleared the 2.716 bar. Against a closed-form expected maximum the same screen would have called the best-of-21,889 comfortably significant; simulating the null is what showed it is not. THE ZERO-COST GATE. The top 60 went through run_e01 anyway so numbers exist rather than resting on the screen. All 60 came back positive on 0 of 9 markets with NO spread charged at all, best pooled zero-cost E among them -0.0992R and worst -0.2454R. That is the gate venue_change.py established as decisive: a rule losing money frictionless cannot be rescued by a cheaper broker, a futures contract, a larger account, or a better fill. TWO STRUCTURAL OBSERVATIONS. The leaders are near-duplicates - z_sma50>0.50 alone, then the same condition paired with upwick<0.50, range_atr>0.10, range_atr<0.90, dnwick<0.90 - which is what a ranking looks like when it sorts noise around one weakly-correlated feature rather than finding distinct effects. And the protocol machinery was itself tested first, on throwaway symlinked copies, because holdout_test.py can run only once: all five paths verified including the one-shot refusal and the hash check. The fourteen crosses remain sealed and unexamined, available to a future question that earns them.

entries.why: market_profile.py measured, across five timeframes on gold and across nine markets at H1, that hours differ enormously in two ways. Cost per unit of movement spans 3.1% to 175.6% depending on hour and timeframe, and the variance ratio spans 0.44 to 2.21 - some hours extend their moves, others give them back. Those are estimates, not selections: every hour is reported and none was chosen for looking good, and the instrument's own tuning log shows the estimates moving 0.00% and 0.05% when knobs that cannot change the measured quantity were varied. Separately, rigorous_search.py has now closed the question of whether a price SHAPE predicts direction here: 0 of 21,889 rules beat a simulated null, and the top 60 lost money at zero cost on 0 of 9 markets. What remains untested is a different claim - that the market's measured STRUCTURE tells you which of two ordinary entries to reach for.
entries.change: Take the hour classification straight off the instrument with no freedom to adjust it: hours with variance ratio >= 1.10 are 'extending', <= 0.90 are 'reverting', and hours costing more than 1.5x the median cost per unit of movement are refused outright as a cost decision. Then run two deliberately ordinary entries through run_e01 - a Donchian-20 close breakout and a 1.5-ATR fade - in the MATCHED arrangement (breakout in extending hours, fade in reverting hours) and in the SWAPPED arrangement (breakout in reverting hours, fade in extending hours). The control is the swap rather than a blind run, because a blind control would differ in trade count as well as in matching, and the matching is the only thing under test. Report the matched-minus-swapped difference per market and pooled across markets.
entries.criterion: One comparison: matched minus swapped, pooled across the nine markets, positive with an across-market |t| clearing the ledger floor. A difference near zero says the regime split is real as a description and empty as a guide - which is a specific falsifiable thing to learn about the instrument and is NOT the same as the map being wrong.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026. The hour classification is computed by the instrument on each market's own history; the entries are fixed in source before the run and neither their parameters nor the VR and cost thresholds are swept.

result.note: REJECTED, and in the direction the instrument's own diagnosis predicts. Matching momentum entries to hours measured as extending and reversion entries to hours measured as reverting came out -0.0172R WORSE than the swapped control, across-market t -1.77, positive on 3 of 9 markets. Per market: XAUUSD -0.0088, XAGUSD -0.0513, EURUSD -0.0093, GBPUSD -0.0277, USDJPY +0.0255, AUDUSD +0.0130, USDCHF -0.0493, USDCAD -0.0511, NZDUSD +0.0043. No single market's difference clears |t| 1.25. WHY IT IS NEGATIVE RATHER THAN ZERO, established from measurements alone. vr_is_illiquidity.py found the variance ratio correlates +0.42/+0.41/+0.41/+0.53 with cost per unit of movement at M1/M5/M15/H1 and runs INVERSELY to movement: the six highest-VR hours on gold H1 cost 1.4x more and move 1.5x less than the six lowest. In a thin book price drifts rather than standing still because nobody is on the other side to push back, and a run of small one-way moves is exactly what a high variance ratio measures - so raw VR cannot separate a trend from an empty book. Matching therefore sent breakouts into the dead expensive end of the day. The size checks out: the cost gap between high-VR and low-VR hours is about 6.3% of range, roughly 0.06R, which is LARGER than the -0.0172R observed. So the cost differential alone more than accounts for the result and there is no need to claim the regime information is anti-predictive - if anything a small positive information content is partly offsetting the cost penalty, though that is not separable at this resolution. TWO THINGS WORTH KEEPING. The map is not refuted: cost per unit of movement spanning 3.1% to 175.6% across hour and timeframe, and the VR-cost correlation itself, are measurements that stand. What is refuted is using RAW VR to choose entries. And on the signal-count question: matched produced 310 signals per market per year, about 2,800 across nine markets, four times the 700/year target. Signal scarcity was never the constraint - each signal loses 0.11R to 0.24R, and producing more of them loses money faster, not slower.

entries.why: The arithmetic of this entire project fits in three numbers. The largest drift-adjusted skill ever measured here is +0.073R, at zero cost. The cost map just measured says H1 charges a median 12.5% of an hour's own range and H4's cheapest hours charge 3.1%. At H1 no measured edge survives; at H4's cheap end a +0.073R gross skill would net around +0.04R. That is the only configuration in 828 hypotheses where the arithmetic is not already lost before the entry rule is chosen, and it comes from the instrument rather than from a search. The regime-matching test just failed at -0.0172R, and its failure was traced to cost rather than to direction - high-variance-ratio hours are the expensive dead ones - which points at the same place.
entries.change: Take the two ordinary entries already fixed in profile_setups.py - a Donchian-20 close breakout and a 1.5-ATR fade, neither re-tuned - and run them on H4 bars restricted to the hours the instrument measures as costing no more than 1.5x the median cost per unit of movement. Refusing the expensive hours is a cost decision and free; the hypothesis is only whether the resulting book is non-negative. Compare against the identical entries on the identical H4 bars with NO hour restriction, so the difference isolates the cost constraint rather than the timeframe change. Report per market and pooled across nine markets, at real bid/ask through run_e01.
entries.criterion: Pooled expectancy at real bid/ask NON-NEGATIVE on the cost-restricted H4 book, with the restricted book beating the unrestricted one by at least the declared margin and an across-market |t| clearing the ledger floor. A restricted book that is still negative says the cost map is correct about which hours are dear and that the edge is too small to survive even the cheapest of them - which closes the timeframe question rather than leaving it open.
entries.test_period: Nine markets, H4 resampled from the H1 cache, 2004-2026. The hour classification is computed by the instrument on each market's own history. Neither entry parameter nor the 1.5x cost threshold is swept.

result.note: REJECTED, and it closes the timeframe question as the criterion said it would. Restricted book -0.1639R, unrestricted -0.1723R, so the cost constraint is worth +0.0084R at t +1.78 - real, consistent in direction, and nowhere near enough. Positive on 0 of 9 markets. 256 signals per market per year restricted. A DESIGN FLAW IN MY OWN TEST, found mid-run and recorded rather than quietly fixed: H4 bars start only at 0, 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20 UTC, so the 24-hour map has six populated cells there and the 1.5x cost cutoff removes exactly one of them (20:00, at 13.51% against a 6.0% median). A constraint that drops one slot in six is barely a constraint, so the per-market differences are mostly sampling noise. I should have checked the cell count before applying a 24-hour map to a six-slot timeframe. THE NUMBER THAT SURVIVES THE FLAW, because it does not depend on the restriction: both H4 arms are as negative as H1's, despite the map measuring H4 at 6.0% of range against H1's 12.5%. The cost saving is cancelled by a gross edge that degrades at the longer horizon - the same conclusion tsmom_d1.py reached at D1 by a different mechanism. AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT REFRAMES ALL OF IT. Running both entries at ZERO cost: momentum -0.0436/-0.0593/-0.0427 at H1 and -0.0175/-0.0558/-0.0492 at H4 on gold/EURUSD/GBPUSD; reversion -0.1221/-0.1217/-0.1129 at H1 and -0.1520/-0.1490/-0.1368 at H4. Every gross expectancy is NEGATIVE. I have repeatedly written in this ledger that the edges here are smaller than the costs. That is wrong. These entries lose money before a single spread is charged, and cost is a penalty stacked on an already-negative base rather than the reason for it. The practical consequence is that the whole cost-reduction avenue - cheaper venue, longer timeframe, affordable hours - cannot help, because zero cost still loses. Reversion is consistently the worse of the two by about 0.09R, which says moves at these horizons continue more than they revert; that is a real directional fact and is NOT a licence to flip the rule, since a bracketed trade's expectancy does not negate when its direction does.

entries.why: bracket_bias.py measured, on random timing at zero cost with an independently written engine that reproduces run_e01 exactly, that this project's standard bracket loses 0.09R to 0.12R per trade before any entry is chosen: -0.0931 on gold, -0.1175 on EURUSD, -0.1090 on GBPUSD. That is larger than the entry skill this repo has ever measured (+0.039 to +0.062R) and larger than its costs (0.011 to 0.073R), and it is present in all 828 prior hypotheses. The cause is the stop width: widening it from 1x to 2x cuts the penalty to -0.0315, a 70% reduction consistent in direction on every market. The martingale guard could never have caught this - a constant-volatility fixture cannot detect a volatility-clustering effect.
entries.change: Re-run the same two ordinary entries - Donchian-20 close breakout and 1.5-ATR fade, neither re-tuned - through the identical engine with stop_mult 2.0 instead of 1.0, at REAL bid/ask, on nine markets H1. Compare against the same entries at stop_mult 1.0 on the same bars, and against matched random timing at both widths so the bracket penalty and the entry skill are reported separately rather than summed. Note in advance that doubling the stop doubles the R denominator, so skill and cost both shrink by roughly half in R terms; the question is whether the penalty falls faster than the skill does.
entries.criterion: Pooled expectancy at real bid/ask NON-NEGATIVE with the 2x stop, and the improvement over the 1x stop clearing the declared margin with an across-market |t| above the ledger floor. A book that improves substantially but stays negative says the bracket was a real and large defect AND that fixing it is still not sufficient - which is a different and more useful finding than either 'it works' or 'nothing changed'.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026 at real bid/ask. The 2x stop was selected from the random-timing control table alone, which never sees the real entries; no entry parameter is swept.

result.note: THE REGISTERED CRITERION FAILS, EVEN THOUGH THIS FILE'S MECHANICS WILL PRINT ACCEPTED. The ledger checks margin and floor, and both are met by a wide margin: improvement +0.0706R against a declared 0.02, across-market t +9.97 against a floor of 4.72, positive on 18 of 18 market-entry pairs. But the criterion written to disk before the run has a third condition the mechanics do not check - pooled expectancy at real bid/ask NON-NEGATIVE - and that fails at -0.0719R with 0 of 18 books positive. Recorded as failing the criterion. THE THREE TERMS, POOLED. net expectancy -0.1425 -> -0.0719 (+0.0706); bracket on random timing -0.1918 -> -0.0806 (+0.1112); entry skill +0.0492 -> +0.0087 (-0.0405). WHAT THAT DECOMPOSITION SAYS, INCLUDING AGAINST ME. The bracket was a real and large defect: halving its penalty improved every one of 18 books. But the entry skill did not merely halve with the doubled R denominator, which is what pure scaling would do - it fell to 18% of its former value, about 35% of what scaling alone predicts. So the skill measured at the 1x stop was substantially an artefact of that tight stop rather than directional information that survives a wider one. This retracts my own reading from earlier in this session, where I reported the entries beating random timing by +0.039 to +0.062 and treated that as evidence the entries carry information. Those numbers were measured through the defective bracket and most of the advantage does not survive its repair. At a fairer bracket these entries have essentially no skill: +0.0087R. AND THE REPAIR IS INCOMPLETE. The bracket at 2x is still -0.0806 on random timing at zero cost, nowhere near zero. Widening the stop halves the penalty; it does not remove it. An R normalised by a per-trade stop distance appears to carry an intrinsic negative expectancy that stop width alone does not fix, and that remains unexplained.

entries.why: The instrument measured a volume-at-price structure that has never been turned into a setup: the value area holds 60% of the daily range, the next day touches the prior day's value area 93.8% of the time, and price closes inside its own value area 66.2% of the time. I reported the 93.8% as a near-tautology baseline - two overlapping daily ranges touch almost by construction - and then never tested anything against it. That is the one part of the original request, to read where volume sits and what each zone does, that produced a measurement and no test. Separately, the bracket work since then means this can be run on a corrected engine: at a 2x stop the random-timing control returns -0.005R once the measured 73.3% stop-first rate is applied, against -0.048R at 1x, so a difference of the size an edge might have is no longer swamped by the exit's own penalty.
entries.change: Compute the prior session's value area and point of control from the instrument's own volume-at-price routine, time-weighted where the volume column is unusable and volume-weighted where it is not, using only data from sessions that have closed. Then test the two opposing readings of that structure, both entered at the next bar's open through run_e01's mechanics at a 2.0x stop: ROTATION - price trades outside the prior value area and then closes back inside it, faded toward the point of control; BREAKOUT - price closes outside the prior value area having been inside it, taken in the direction of the break. Each against matched random timing with its own invalidation levels, nine markets H1, real bid/ask, with the three terms - net expectancy, bracket penalty, entry skill - reported separately rather than summed.
entries.criterion: Either reading, pooled across nine markets, showing drift-adjusted skill positive with an across-market |t| clearing the ledger floor AND net expectancy at real bid/ask non-negative. Both readings failing says the value-area structure is real as a description of where price spends its time and carries no directional information at this horizon - which is the same shape of answer the variance ratio gave, and would say the instrument's zone output is descriptive rather than predictive.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026 at real bid/ask, 2.0x stop. Value areas are computed per session on closed data only; no zone parameter is swept and the 70% value-area definition is the instrument's existing one.

result.note: BOTH READINGS FAIL THE CRITERION, BUT NOT IN THE WAY THE CRITERION ANTICIPATED, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS. Rotation: net E -0.0670, bracket -0.0976, skill +0.0306, across-market t +2.52, skill positive on 7 of 9, expectancy positive on 0 of 9, 93 signals per market per year. Breakout: net E -0.0566, bracket -0.0772, skill +0.0206, t +2.28, skill positive on 8 of 9, expectancy positive on 1 of 9, 115 signals per market per year. Neither t clears the 4.72 floor and neither book is profitable, so the registered criterion fails on both of its conditions. WHERE THE CRITERION WAS WRONG. It said that both readings failing would mean the value-area structure carries no directional information. That is not what the numbers say: skill is positive on 7 of 9 and 8 of 9 markets respectively, which is not an absence of information. THE OBSERVATION THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS, AND IT UNDERCUTS BOTH READINGS. These two setups are near-opposite - rotation fires on re-entry into the prior value area and fades toward the point of control, breakout fires on exit from it and follows the break - and BOTH show positive skill. If the value area carried directional information, one should win and the other should lose by a similar amount. Both winning says the measured skill is probably not directional at all but something the two share: each fires only when price is moving relative to the prior session's zone, while the random control enters at any time including dead ones. That would make the +0.03 a selection effect for being in the market when it moves, not a statement about which way it goes - which is exactly why it cannot pay the bracket penalty and the spread, since knowing that something will happen is not knowing its sign. That explanation is consistent with the data and UNTESTED; it is recorded as the reading to check next, not as a conclusion. On the standing signal-count target: these produce 837 and 1,035 signals a year across nine markets, either side of the 700 asked for, and both lose money.

entries.why: Every positive skill number in this session was measured against a control that randomises TIMING only. Two results now suggest that control is too weak. First, the ordinary momentum and reversion entries both beat it. Second, and more tellingly, the value-area rotation and breakout setups are near-opposite readings of the same structure - one fades re-entry toward the point of control, the other follows the break away - and BOTH beat it, on 7 of 9 and 8 of 9 markets. If the value area carried directional information one should win and the other lose by a similar amount. Both winning says the measured skill is probably not directional at all, but something the two share: each fires only when price is moving relative to a prior zone, while a timing-only control enters at any bar including dead ones. That would make every +0.02 to +0.05 skill figure in this session a selection effect for being in the market when it moves rather than a statement about which way.
entries.change: Replace the timing-only control with one matched on MOVEMENT. For each real signal record its own bar's true range over ATR, bin those into deciles, then draw the control's entries from bars in the same decile in the same proportions, so the control sits in equally active conditions and differs from the real rule only in direction and level. Run it against four setup families already measured - Donchian-20 momentum, 1.5-ATR fade, value-area rotation, value-area breakout - on nine markets H1 at the 2.0x stop, and report skill against BOTH controls side by side so the drop is visible per family rather than asserted.
entries.criterion: If the skill measured against the timing-only control largely survives the volatility-matched one, it is directional information and every prior skill figure stands. If it collapses toward zero across all four families, then the controls used throughout this session were too weak and those figures measured activity selection rather than direction - which would retract the skill readings in the regime-matched, wider-stop and value-area entries alike. A mixed result, surviving in some families and not others, identifies which measurements to keep.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026, real bid/ask, 2.0x stop - the same books already measured, re-run against a stronger control rather than on new data.

result.note: THE CONTROL USED THROUGHOUT THIS SESSION WAS TOO WEAK, AND 91% OF EVERY SKILL FIGURE IT PRODUCED WAS ACTIVITY SELECTION. Skill measured against a timing-only control versus against one matched on the signal bar's own true-range decile: momentum +0.0253 -> +0.0049 (20% retained, t +0.63, positive on 6 of 9); reversion -0.0079 -> -0.0186 (already negative, worse); value-area rotation +0.0306 -> +0.0005 (2% retained, t +0.08, 5 of 9); value-area breakout +0.0206 -> +0.0191 (93% retained, t +1.77, 7 of 9). Across all four families +0.0171 -> +0.0015, nine percent retained. WHAT THIS RETRACTS, INCLUDING THINGS I CALLED ENCOURAGING. The regime-matched entry skill, the +0.0492 skill in the wider-stop comparison, and the value-area rotation skill were all measured against timing-only controls and are mostly not directional information. A rule that fires only when something is happening beats a control that enters at any bar including dead ones, without knowing which way the something goes. The tell was already visible and I named it before running this: rotation and breakout are near-opposite readings of one structure and BOTH beat the timing control, which cannot happen if the structure carries direction. THE SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THIS SESSION. run_e01_control, used across this repo's 830 hypotheses, randomises timing with matched risk ratios - dist over ATR - which matches trade GEOMETRY but not the activity level of the bar the signal fired on. Every skill number in this project that leans on it inherits the same weakness. I am not restating those results here; I am recording that the instrument they used has a measured 91% inflation on the four families tested. WHAT PARTIALLY SURVIVES. Value-area breakout retains 93% of its skill at +0.0191 with t +1.77 on 7 of 9 markets. That is the only family where the effect looks directional rather than selectional, and it is still far below the 4.72 floor and still cannot pay the bracket penalty and the spread.

entries.why: Audit check 8 measured that random_like builds a control whose stop sits a third as far away as the rule's - dist/ATR median 0.559 against 1.638 - so R, which divides by that distance, is scaled differently in the two books. Every skill figure in bracket_bias, wider_stop, value_area_setups and vol_matched_control was read across that gap, and the vol_matched_control result that 91% of apparent skill was activity selection was itself measured through the defective control. Both the claim and its retraction rest on the same broken instrument, so neither currently stands. The four families have to be re-measured through a control that inherits the rule's geometry before anything about them can be said.
entries.change: Replace random_like with controls.py, which for each real signal records its own dist/ATR ratio, draws a donor bar from a matched stratum, and SYNTHESISES an invalidation level at that same ratio on the donor bar - so the two books have identical risk geometry by construction. Run all eight levels C0 through C7 on the four families momentum, reversion, value-area rotation and value-area breakout, across the nine-market H1 panel at real bid/ask with a 2.0x stop. The decision quantity is skill against C7 - structure-context matched with direction randomised - which is the only level that requires knowing which way rather than merely when.
entries.criterion: A family carries directional information only if its skill against C7 is positive with a cross-market t above the floor the cumulative hypothesis count implies, currently 4.72. Skill against C1 that does not survive to C7 is activity, session or regime selection and is reported as such with the level named. If no family clears C7, the finding is that these four families carry no directional information at this horizon once geometry, timing, activity, volatility, session, regime and range position are all held constant - and the earlier 91%-retraction figure is superseded by a number measured on a correct instrument rather than merely repeated.
entries.test_period: Nine markets H1 2004-2026, real bid/ask, 2.0x stop - the same books, re-measured through a corrected control rather than on new data. No holdout is touched.

result.note: REJECTED. No family carries directional information at C7, and the strongest is reversion at t -0.14; all four are NEGATIVE against the strongest control. By family, skill against C7: momentum -0.0116 (t -1.28, positive on 2 of 9); reversion -0.0011 (t -0.14, 4 of 9); value-area rotation -0.0056 (t -0.95, 3 of 9); value-area breakout -0.0094 (t -1.17, 3 of 9). THE EARLIER NUMBERS WERE MOSTLY INSTRUMENT. vol_matched_control measured +0.0171 against a timing-only control. On the cleaned frame with a geometry-matched control the same quantity is +0.0026 to +0.0066, and at one family it is negative. Two defects account for the difference and both are now fixed: random_like took the random bar's own high or low as the invalidation level, so its stop sat a third as far from entry as the rule's while R divides by that distance; and 29% of every bar in the sample was a weekend or rollover hour the venue did not quote, which collapsed Wilder ATR to 6.5% of its Thursday level by Sunday and made the engine reject 84.8% of Monday bars against 56.9% of Thursday's. THE 91% ACTIVITY-SELECTION CLAIM IS SUPERSEDED, NOT CONFIRMED. A synthetic rule that selects busy bars and faces a coin shows no skill at any level once geometry is matched - |t| below 2 at all eight, C1 included. There was no activity artifact to remove; the 91% was the geometry gap. WHAT THE PROFILE SHOWS INSTEAD. Several levels are significantly NEGATIVE: momentum against session-matched -0.0095 t -2.79 on 1 of 9; reversion against C5 -0.0113 t -2.63; value-area rotation against regime-matched -0.0149 t -3.16 on 1 of 9; value-area breakout against C5 -0.0190 t -2.91 on 1 of 9. All four families do systematically WORSE than matched random entries. The mechanism is measured rather than guessed: R divides by a stop distance set from ATR, these rules fire on high-ATR bars, and a larger denominator earns a smaller R for the same price move. Under this normalisation selecting volatile moments is a cost. That makes R-through-a-bracket a poor instrument for asking whether directional information exists, which is the next thing to separate.
